findings.issue: Personal «a» marks the relative as a direct object while «en él» already renders בּוֹ; same person, extra government.
Qal רחץ has no object and no reflexive stem; «se» specifies that he washes himself.
Qal טמא is a state of being unclean; «se impurecerá» is inchoative and can be heard as self-caused impurity.
«tarde» spans afternoon through dusk; the token is the evening.

notes: Person, number, and the three wash verbs stay distinct; dual hands remain hands.
